name: TLS certificate validation disabled / accept-any-cert
task_triggers: debugging TLS handshake or self-signed cert errors
attack_scenario: An on-path attacker presents a self-signed or attacker-controlled certificate; because the chain is never validated, the app completes the handshake with the attacker, who then decrypts and modifies all 'HTTPS' traffic including credentials.
negative_test_hint: present a self-signed certificate for "attacker.example.com" during the handshake and assert the challenge is cancelled instead of completing the connection

exemplar.explanation: Setting kCFStreamSSLValidatesCertificateChain to false or using the private setAllowsAnyHTTPSCertificate:YES turns off X.509 chain validation, so any certificate, including an on-path attacker's self-signed one, is accepted and the whole 'HTTPS' channel is open to MITM. Evaluating SecTrust and cancelling the challenge on failure keeps the connection pinned to a valid, trusted chain.
